module_title: Advanced Analysis - Suspension of Rights, Judicial Review, and Special Provisions
introduction: This advanced level analyzes the complex relationship between Emergency powers and Fundamental Rights (Articles 358 & 359), the scope of judicial review, and the special provisions granted to specific states under the 371 series.

core_concepts.title: Suspension of Article 19 (Article 358)
core_concepts.description: When a National Emergency is declared on grounds of 'war or external aggression' (External Emergency), the six freedoms under Article 19 are automatically suspended. However, they are NOT suspended if the emergency is based on 'armed rebellion' (Internal Emergency).

core_concepts.title: Suspension of Other Rights (Article 359)
core_concepts.description: Authorizes the President to suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights during a National Emergency. However, the rights themselves are not suspended, only their enforcement is.

core_concepts.title: The Immortal Articles (20 & 21)
core_concepts.description: The 44th Amendment made it unconstitutional to suspend Articles 20 (protection in respect of conviction) and 21 (right to life and personal liberty) under any circumstances, even during a National Emergency.

core_concepts.title: Special Provisions (Articles 371 to 371J)
core_concepts.description: Part XXI contains special temporary, transitional, and special provisions for states like Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, and Karnataka to protect their cultural/economic interests.

important_entities.name: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)
important_entities.significance: A landmark Supreme Court verdict which held that the imposition of President's Rule is subject to Judicial Review. It ruled that the state assembly cannot be dissolved until Parliament approves the emergency.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: UPSC frequently tests this: Art 358 applies ONLY to external emergencies and is automatic. Art 359 applies to BOTH external and internal emergencies but requires a specific Presidential order detailing which rights' enforcement is suspended.
Remember that while Article 370 (Special Status to J&K) is still in the Constitution text, it was effectively rendered inoperative in 2019, and J&K was reorganized into two Union Territories.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps map the letters to states: 371A(Nagaland), 371B(Assam), 371C(Manipur), 371D/E(Andhra/Telangana), 371F(Sikkim), 371G(Mizoram), 371H(Arunachal), 371I(Goa), 371J(Karnataka).

exam_strategy_tips: In Assertion-Reasoning, critically analyze statements claiming 'Fundamental Rights are suspended during an emergency'. Technically, under 359, it's the *enforcement* that is suspended, not the rights themselves.
State PCS and UPSC Prelims love matching questions for Articles 371A to 371J. Memorize the alphabet-state mappings perfectly.
